title: Auto-exposure super bright while resizing the Editor window
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: v4.4.1.stable.official [49a5bc7b6]

### System information

Godot v4.4.1.stable - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1060 6GB (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.6094) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-8500 CPU @ 3.00GHz (6 threads)

### Issue description

When using a WorldEnvironment node with either physical or practical CameraAttributes with auto exposure enabled, resizing the editor's 3d preview (by either resizing the whole application or by adjusting the size of the docks such as the inspector or the shader editor) results in an ultra-bright screen, until the auto exposure has readjusted.

I believe that this is caused by the auto exposure constantly refreshing during the resize. I'm not sure if this is intended, but it might make sense to only update the auto exposure once the window size is no longer being changed.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e5cf28de-9a1d-440a-9382-53e307494fa0

### Steps to reproduce

With MRP:
- Open minimal reproduction project
- Open `scene.tscn`
- Resize application window or editor docks to see the issue

Without MRP:
- Create 3D scene
- Add world environment
- Add camera attributes
- Enable auto exposure
- Resize application window or editor docks to see the issue

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[godot_auto_exposure_mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/19516878/godot_auto_exposure_mrp.zip)
